R0284.title: Market Information Manipulation
R0284.definition: Attackers forge, amplify, pollute, or delay market information to affect price discovery, trading decisions, sentiment judgment, or risk assessment.
R0284.description:
Market information manipulation covers false news, informal rumor essays, AI-generated minutes or research reports, deepfake content, social-media manipulation, sentiment pollution, information-latency attacks, and information-synchronization-gap exploitation. Attackers may impersonate issuers, analysts, media outlets, traders, or experts to create information capable of affecting trading judgment.

This differs from generic false content. The focus is information used to change market expectations and trading behavior. AI-generated content, deepfakes, and cross-platform dissemination lower the cost of fabrication, making rumors, false reports, and delayed information easier to amplify within trading windows.
R0284.influence: It distorts market expectations, misleads investors, creates abnormal price volatility, damages reputation, and creates regulatory risk.

references.title: NIST Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)

observables: Suspected false messages spread rapidly around trading windows with price moves
AI-generated reports or minutes lack verifiable sources yet are amplified
The same narrative is synchronized by linked accounts across platforms
Information used for trading differs from authoritative disclosure in timing or content
